writing.exampleCaption: The data lives inside the lock, so unlocked access is unrepresentable.
writing.explanation: Arc<T> is Rc with an atomic count so it can cross threads. Mutex<T> holds the data itself rather than guarding it by convention, so the only way to reach the value is to lock — and the guard unlocks when it drops, which means a forgotten unlock is not a bug you can write.
writing.feedback: Rc uses a non-atomic count; Arc is the thread-safe version.
writing.question: Why can that Rc not cross the thread boundary?
writing.rule: The lock guard unlocks on drop, so there is no unlock to forget.

writing.summary: Arc shares the value; Mutex makes mutation through it safe.
